title: Protein crystals
subtitle: A better suspension starts with its structure.
opportunity: Control crystal size and distribution to make concentrated protein suspensions easier to handle. Pembrolizumab is our evidence anchor, not a qualified product of this project.
evidence: A 2019 flight study reported more homogeneous crystals and lower suspension viscosity. Insights from the flight also improved Earth processing.
test: Reproduce the strongest ground recipe, compare independent flight and Earth batches, and measure viscosity, size distribution, stability and retained protein function.
hardware: Sealed, sterile solution-growth cartridge with controlled temperature history and optical monitoring.

title: Drug crystals
subtitle: Explore a different solid form.
opportunity: Use controlled crystallization to investigate useful drug solid forms. A different crystal form may change stability or dissolution, but the useful property must be demonstrated.
evidence: Varda recovered orbital ritonavir Form III; a 2026 paper studies its stability. This is an external operator’s result, not our experiment or a partnership.
test: Compare form identity, purity, dissolution, stability and batch reproducibility against optimized terrestrial crystallization under matched analytical methods.
hardware: Chemically compatible sealed cell, temperature program and nucleation control. Solvent handling and return preservation need separate qualification.

title: Cooling materials
subtitle: Engineer the transition. Test the cycle.
opportunity: Investigate whether solidification under reduced convection produces microstructures useful for barocaloric cooling. NPG-based systems offer a research starting point.
evidence: NPG–camphor solidification has been studied in microgravity. Separate Earth studies show NPG barocaloric behavior; the flight study does not establish better cooling performance.
test: Measure thermal hysteresis, caloric response and durability over repeated cycles. Compare with preconditioned Earth controls and test whether any structural advantage persists.
hardware: Dedicated gradient furnace and thermal sensors, with enough isolation and heat-rejection margin to protect neighboring experiments.
constraint: Heat load & structure survival in cycling

title: MOF membranes
subtitle: Build selectivity, one pore at a time.
opportunity: Grow metal–organic framework layers with controlled orientation and fewer transport defects. Selective lithium recovery is one functional target to evaluate.
evidence: Orbital MOF research motivates the growth question. Lithium-selective UiO-67 transport has been demonstrated on Earth; an orbital selectivity advantage remains unproven.
test: Measure ion selectivity, flux, adhesion, fouling and lifetime against optimized ground membranes, including relevant microfluidic growth controls.
hardware: A precursor-compatible solution cell with a dedicated substrate mount, temperature control and sealed wetted paths.

title: Photonic crystals
subtitle: Let order shape the light.
opportunity: Assemble ordered colloidal structures for optical elements. Reduced settling can enable large ordered domains; the next challenge is a stable, useful optical material.
evidence: The ACE-T11 study reports a large FCC colloidal crystal grown on the ISS and returned to Earth. It motivates optical applications without establishing a finished-device advantage.
test: Quantify defects, scattering, optical loss and reproducibility after stabilization and return. Compare with the best practical Earth self-assembly process.
hardware: Quiet colloidal assembly cell, controlled temperature and concentration, calibrated optical metrology and a stabilization step.
